title: Okra soup
lead:
{{Short description|Soup prepared with okra}}
[[File:Sayur oyong.JPG|thumb|260px|Indonesian ''[[List of Indonesian soups#Sayur (vegetable soups)|sayur oyong]]'' (okra soup) in clear light broth]]

'''Okra''' or '''Okro''' {{Audio|LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Vivian Amalachukwu-Okro.wav|Listen|help=no}} is a soup made from the pods of the [[Okra|Okra plant]], cooked in a wide variety of ways across several cultures and continents. As a term, the word 'Okra' ('''English''') said to be borrowed from '''Igbo''',<ref name=":0" /> is believed to have originated from a West African language in the Americas, from the [[Igbo people]] of Nigeria — "Ọkwụrụ/Ọ́kụ̀rụ̀."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oed.com/dictionary/okra_n?tl=true|title=okra, n. meanings, etymology and more | Oxford English Dictionary|website=www.oed.com}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://www.oed.com/dictionary/okra_n?tl=true |title=Okra, n. |website=Oxford English Dictionary |accessdate=2025-07-10 |quote="The word 'okra' is probably a borrowing from the Igbo language, where it is known as 'ọ́kùrù.'"}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/okra|title=Definition of OKRA|date=September 3, 2026|website=www.merriam-webster.com}}</ref>. 

The soup is prepared using the edible green seed pods of the [[okra]] flowering plant as a primary ingredient. Other [[vegetable]]s can be added to the soup as well, such as Jute leaf or Ugu leaf. Depending on the specific variant being prepared, okra soup can have a clear broth or be deep green in colour, much like the okra plant itself. Okra (and, by extension, okra soup) can have a slippery or "slimy" [[mouthfeel]]. The [[edible]] green seed pods can also be used in other stews and soups, such as the [[American cuisine|American]] dish [[gumbo]].<ref>{{cite book | last=Walker | first=S.S. | title=African Roots/American Cultures: Africa in the Creation of the Americas | publisher=Rowman & Littlefield Publishers | year=2001 | isbn=978-0-7425-0165-2 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EJzHiqBPJCoC&pg=PA64 | page=64}}</ref>
